answer: Each identity requires 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard computation to solve a unique prism-structured hashing challenge, serving as a bright lantern for detecting sybil activity. An honest agent spends significant time filling the memory terrace, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000,000 gigabytes of effort, rendering mass replication prohibitively costly. Verifiers audit logs for duplicate memory access patterns; evidence of shared work triggers immediate, non-refundable identity revocation.
